summary: Segmented request pin split during orchestrator priority inversion causes hybrid fallback for a subset of tenant traffic
description: Issue summary: During a weighted canary drain window in us-east (dedicated pool for ArcWave Health) a subset of segmented, chunked requests from the same tenant were routed to a fallback hybrid path (legacy variant + degraded quantized variant) while other segments kept the pinned model. Impact: partial degradation of inference quality and billing spike for the customer because some segments hit a higher-cost fallback and produced tokenization deltas. This appears tied to an orchestrator priority inversion that reordered hook commits for segmented requests and produced a split pin state across the routing mesh.
impact: Multiple long-running chat sessions for ArcWave Health experienced mixed-model outputs for ~7 minutes (approx 3% of edge requests for the tenant). Customers reported quality regressions and one alert from their integration tests. No total outage; degraded correctness and cost increase.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Provision a dedicated tenant pool with pinned rw-v2-13b-quant and enable segmented/chunked streaming on the client.
2) Trigger a staged canary drain with staggered prewarm and priority hooks (simulate autoscaler-induced preempt).
3) Send multi-chunk sessions at 120 rpm to observe routing divergence.
4) Observe routing traces and routing-mesh epoch for split pin markers.
observed_behavior: Some segments in single sessions were routed to the legacy variant due to an edge-to-orchestrator commit reorder; other segments maintained the pinned variant. The edge proxy logs show different routing decisions within the same session id; orchestrator commit traces show priority hooks applied out-of-order during a preemptive rollback path.
expected_behavior: Pin commit/rollback ordering must be consistent per-session (session-scoped consensus) so segmented requests never observe mixed pinned and fallback variants. Rollback/priority hooks must not produce partial pin states for ongoing sessions.

temporary_workaround: We applied a traffic quarantine rule at the ingress level to pin ArcWave Health traffic to the dedicated serving pool (force primary variant) while we roll a hotfix. This reduced the mixed outputs but increased tail latency for a brief period. Customers were notified and offered credits for the impacted window.
investigation_notes: 03-05 03:30 - Initial triage by support: confirmed customer reports and collected traces. Notified SRE and Orchestrator on-call (#support & #orchestrator).

03-05 04:10 - Reproduced split-pin in staging by simulating preemptive hook reorder with the orchestrator dev tool. Hypothesis: priority inversion when rollback hook runs earlier than scheduled commit for some request segments.
03-05 06:00 - SRE reproduced an internal-only variant: ordering inversion occurs when two hooks with adjacent commit windows and different priorities overlap under a prewarm drain.
03-06 09:20 - Suggested mitigation: make session-scoped commit idempotent and add segment-atomic pin check at the edge. Draft PRs created to edge-proxy and orchestrator.
03-08 14:40 - Performance team flagged potential latency regression if we add segment-atomic checks; recommend targeted patch limited to segmented streaming paths for now.
03-09 11:00 - Deployed temporary ingress quarantine and a conservative canary rollback to stop further splits. Monitoring shows split rate dropped to zero after quarantine.

SRE Pager (2026-03-06): Quarantine rule applied at 2026-03-06T02:15Z. ArcWave traffic pinned to primary while fix is prepared. Customer notified: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/CUST-arcwave/ping123
Support Lead (2026-03-08): Confirmed mitigation reduced impact. Need code fix and an e2e canary to prevent regressions. Please link PRs and confluence pages for postmortem.
root_cause: Priority inversion in orchestrator hook processing combined with lack of segment-atomic pin reconciliation at the edge. Under certain overlapping hook windows a rollback hook could be applied to early segments while later segments still committed, producing split pin state across the routing mesh for the same session.
next_steps: 1) Backport orchestrator hook ordering guard to the stable branch (PR #1229). 2) Add a lightweight segment-atomic pin verification in edge-proxy for chunked/streaming sessions (PR #807). 3) Add an e2e canary test that simulates overlapping hook windows and segmented streaming. 4) Run a targeted rollback test in us-east with telemetry gated. 5) Draft customer post-incident note and credit reconciliation.
resolution: Partial mitigation completed: ingress quarantine reduced splits; code PRs opened for orchestrator and edge-proxy. Full fix pending code review and performance verification. Planned deployment: 2026-03-12 (canary) -> 2026-03-15 (regional deploy), pending approval.
notes_for_postmortem: Include measurements: percent of sessions affected, billing delta, and canary test specs. Validate that segment-atomic checks don't add >2% p99 latency. Cross-team owners: orchestrator, edge-proxy, serving-runtime. Postmortem page to be created after full fix rollout.
